what: Old Republic writes two unrelated kinds of insurance: title insurance on American property transactions, and specialty commercial insurance for trucking, construction and financial risks.
customers: Home buyers and lenders at closing, and businesses buying commercial cover through independent agents.
money: commercial property and casualty, especially trucking and construction
title policies and escrow on property transactions
moat: Title plants of property records assembled over a century, and specialty underwriting niches where pricing requires loss data a newcomer does not have.
risks: Title revenue collapses when house sales fall, as they have with high mortgage rates
Commercial insurance pricing has been softening after several strong years
Only two analysts cover the stock
opportunities: 8.9 times earnings and 8.3 times free cash flow with $1.1B of free cash flow
Revenue recovered from $7.3B to $9.1B in two years
Almost no debt at $193M, and the company has paid a dividend for over eighty years
watch: Title order volumes and the combined ratio in general insurance.
